# Introduction
* **Multi-Model:** GPT-5.6, Claude Fable 5.1, fast models. Amp uses them all, for what each model is
best at.
* **Orbs:** Machines that Amp creates per thread, with your code, tools, and plugins already set
up. Send a prompt, close your laptop, and the agent keeps working.
* **Everywhere:** Start an orb from your iPhone, check on it from your Mac, and follow up in
the TUI. The apps notify you when a thread is ready for your next message.
* **Opinionated:** You’re always using the good parts of Amp. If we don’t use and love a feature,
we kill it.
* **On the Frontier:** Amp goes where the models take it. No backward compatibility, no legacy
features.
* **Threads:** You can save and share your interactions with Amp.
_Want to go much deeper? Follow along on our Raising an Agent podcast and the Chronicle time capsules where we share what we’re learning as we build Amp._

## Quickstart
2. [2 Connect Your ChatGPT Subscription Optional Use your ChatGPT Plus or Pro subscription for OpenAI models in Amp.](https://ampcode.com/settings/model-routing?add=chatgpt-sub)
3. [3 Add Your Code Create a project from a Git repository, or start without one.](https://ampcode.com/projects?newProject=1)
4.
4 Run an Agent in an Orb Give Amp a task in a fresh cloud environment with your project ready.
5. 5 Get the macOS & iOS Apps Install Amp on your Mac, iPhone, and iPad to follow your agents anywhere.
6. 6 Use Amp on the CLI Install Amp and work with it from your terminal.

## Explore
Amp is the same agent and the same threads everywhere. Pick where you want to work:
* **Web.** ampcode.com needs no install. Start a thread, and Amp works in an orb , a machine it creates for that thread.
* **Mac, iPhone, and iPad.** The macOS & iOS apps add notifications,
  dictation, and sharing from other apps.
* **Terminal.** The CLI runs Amp on your own machine, in your editor’s terminal, or
  from scripts.

Docs Chronicle Using Amp

# Getting Started

The Amp CLI runs in your terminal. It can run the Amp agent on your machine, in an orb , or on a connected runner .

The CLI supports macOS, Linux, and Windows through WSL. On Windows, we recommend [WezTerm](https://wezterm.org/install/windows.html) or [Alacritty](https://alacritty.org/) instead of Windows Terminal for fully functional clipboard
support.

## Install

Here’s how you can install the Amp CLI:

Install

Mac/Linux/WSL Windows Homebrew

Mac/Linux/WSL Windows Homebrew

curl -fsSL https://ampcode.com/install.sh | bash

If your workspace has its own installation instructions, sign in and open the install page . Amp will show the instructions for that workspace.

## Use the CLI

After installing, run `amp` to start the Amp CLI.

Without any arguments, it runs in interactive mode:

```
$ amp
```

If you pipe input to the CLI, it uses the input as the first user message in interactive mode:

```
$ echo "commit all my changes" |  amp
```

To see more of what the CLI can do, run `amp --help` .

## Shell Completions

Amp provides Tab completion for commands, aliases, options, and declared argument choices in
Bash, Zsh, Fish, and PowerShell. Setup reads the command definitions from the installed Amp version.
Pressing Tab runs a small JavaScript resolver with Amp’s bundled Bun runtime, without starting
the Amp application. You do not need Usage, a separate Bun installation, or a command spec.
Completions work without signing in or connecting to the network.

For Bash 4 or later, install and load [bash-completion](https://github.com/scop/bash-completion) ,
then add this line to `~/.bashrc` after loading it:

```
source < ( amp completions  bash )
```

For Zsh, add this line to `~/.zshrc` after your existing `compinit` call. If you have not enabled
Zsh completions, first run `autoload -Uz compinit; compinit` in that file.

```
source <(amp completions zsh)
```

For Fish, add this to `~/.config/fish/config.fish` :

```
if status is-interactive
    amp completions fish | source
end
```

For PowerShell 7, add this line to your `$PROFILE` file:

```
amp completions pwsh | Out-String | Invoke-Expression
```

Open a new shell or run the setup line in your current shell. Remove any earlier Amp completion
setup to avoid conflicts. After updating Amp, open a new shell or run the setup line again to
refresh the command definitions. Amp does not change your shell configuration.

## Attach Images

Press `Ctrl+V` to paste an image from your clipboard into the prompt.
Use `Ctrl+V` , not `Cmd+V` , even on macOS. You can also drag and drop image files
from your file manager into the terminal to attach them.

If your terminal intercepts `Ctrl+V` , press `Ctrl+O` and run `prompt: paste image from clipboard` . See CLI Keybindings for more shortcuts.

## Choose Where the Thread Runs

By default, `amp` starts a local thread. Use `--executor` to open the interactive TUI with a new
thread that will run locally, in an orb, or on one of your runners :

```
$ amp  --executor local $ amp  --executor  orb $ amp  --executor  runner:grandmas-garage-server
```

Orb threads use the Amp project that matches the current directory’s Git remote. If no project
matches, Amp warns you and uses a no-project orb. A runner ID identifies a connected runner started
with `amp --no-tui --runner-id <id>` .

## Update

Amp automatically checks and installs new versions in the background. You don’t have to do anything except regularly restart Amp.

You can also manually check for updates:

```
amp update
```

You can check which version you have by running:

```
amp version
```

## Connect an Editor

Amp can connect to VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Zed, and Neovim. Open the editor, run `amp` , then open the command palette with `Ctrl+O` and select `ide connect` .

The integration lets Amp:

* See the current open file and selection, so Amp can better understand the context of your prompt
* Edit files through your IDE, with full undo support

Neovim also requires the [Amp Neovim plugin](https://github.com/ampcode/amp.nvim) .

Previous Desktop Next Keybindings

## Assistant

You are currently inside **Amp’s terminal chat interface**.

Amp is basically:

```diagram
You describe a coding task
          ↓
Amp reads files, runs commands, edits code, and tests it
          ↓
You review the answer and Git changes
```

Important concepts:

- **Prompt:** Write normal English—not shell commands. Example:  
  `Find why login fails, fix it, and run the tests.`
- **Thread:** One conversation/task. Start a new thread for unrelated work.
- **Local thread:** Amp works directly in the folder where you launched it. Here, that is `C:\Users\donal\projects\AgentIDE`.
- **Orb:** A separate cloud machine containing a checkout of your project.
- **Tools:** Commands Amp can execute, such as reading files, editing code, running tests, and searching documentation.
- **Nothing is automatically committed or pushed** unless you ask. Local file edits do happen immediately.

A normal workflow is:

```text
cd path/to/project
amp
> Explain what this project does. Do not change anything.
> Fix the bug in the settings screen and test it.
> Show me exactly what you changed.
> Commit these changes.
```

Useful controls:

- `Enter` — send your message

The simplest mental model: **Amp is a coding employee operating a terminal—not a traditional command-line program with commands you must memorize. Tell it the outcome you want.**

Official guide: [Getting Started with the Amp CLI](https://ampcode.com/docs/cli).

# CLI Keybindings

Amp’s most important keyboard shortcut is `Ctrl+O` to open the command palette:

The Amp CLI command palette showing available commands

Other shortcuts worth remembering:

* `Ctrl+G` opens the current prompt in your editor. This requires `$EDITOR`.
* `Ctrl+V` pastes an image from the clipboard, even on macOS (not `Cmd+V` ).
* `Ctrl+S` turns the Dial before a thread's first message. After that, it
  shows the thread's mode, which cannot change.
* `Ctrl+R` opens your prompt history.
* `↑` and `↓` move to queued and previous messages so you can edit them.
* `Alt+T` expands thinking and tool blocks.
* `Alt+D` toggles reasoning effort for the active model where supported.
* `Alt+R` toggles fast mode for the active model.
* `Ctrl+C` `Ctrl+N` archives the current thread and starts a new one.
* `Ctrl+C` `Ctrl+E` archives the current thread and quits.
* `Ctrl+C` `Ctrl+C` quits.
* `Esc` `Esc` interrupts the active agent turn.
* `@` mentions files.

You can also drag and drop image files from your file manager into the terminal to attach them
to your prompt. If your terminal intercepts `Ctrl+V` , press `Ctrl+O` and run `prompt: paste image from clipboard` .

To see the full map of keyboard shortcuts and all available commands, run:

```
amp config keymap
```

For app and web shortcuts, see Keyboard Shortcuts in your personal settings.

## Writing Prompts

When you’re in the prompt editor in the CLI, `Enter` submits your prompt.

If the agent is still working, `Enter` steers it by default: your message is delivered
after the current step instead of waiting for the agent to completely finish. To queue the message
until the agent finishes instead, press `Ctrl+O` and run `prompt: queue message` (type `queue` ). Press `Enter` `Enter` on a queued message to steer it sooner. You can
make queueing the default under Settings → Advanced → Default Message Send Behavior .
See Queueing Messages .

Use `Shift+Enter` to insert a newline when your terminal supports modified Enter keys, for
example Ghostty, WezTerm, Kitty, iTerm2, or tmux with `extended-keys` enabled.

Amp knows how to configure tmux for this, so you can ask Amp to set it up.

Use `Ctrl+J` to insert a newline in any terminal.

You can also type `\` followed by `Return` to insert a newline.

If you have the environment variable `$EDITOR` set, you can use `Ctrl+G` or the `editor` command from the command palette to open your editor to write a prompt.

## Amp CLI in tmux

Tmux will not distinguish `Shift+Enter` from `Enter` by default. In order for `Shift+Enter` to insert a newline in the Amp CLI, enable `extended-keys` in your tmux config.

If you don’t want to change tmux settings, use `Ctrl+J` to insert a newline instead.

```
$ tmux  set -s  extended-keys on
```

To make it persistent, add `set -s extended-keys on` to `~/.tmux.conf` , then reload: `tmux source-file ~/.tmux.conf` .

Amp knows how to configure tmux for this, so you can ask Amp to set it up.

## Customize the Keymap

Use the `amp.keymap` setting to customize CLI keybindings:

```
{ "amp.keymap" : { "mode.toggle" : [ "ctrl+s" , "ctrl+j" ] , "thread.copyURL" : "<leader> u" , "thread.interrupt" : [ "esc esc" , "ctrl+l" ] } }
```

Separate keys with spaces to define a chord, such as `ctrl+c ctrl+e` . The key `<leader> u` means pressing `Ctrl+X` and then `u` . To change the `<leader>` key, define a keymap entry for `"leader"` .

Configuring a command replaces its default key or chord. Use an array to keep the old shortcut and add another one. Set a command’s entry to `null` to unbind its default.

Unlike other settings, keymaps in your user settings file at `~/.config/amp/settings.json` override workspace entries in `.amp/settings.json` .

## Assistant

That is an Amp UI bug/terminal compatibility problem—not you using it incorrectly.

Try these in order:

1. Press `Esc`.
2. Press `Ctrl+O` to open the command palette; this may clear the tip.
3. Resize the terminal window; overlays often redraw and disappear.
4. Quit with `Ctrl+C`, `Ctrl+C`, then restart `amp`.

`Ctrl+.` is not reliably transmitted by many Windows terminals. Amp officially supports Windows through WSL and recommends WezTerm or Alacritty; your current terminal may never send that key combination correctly.

If the tip persists, use `Ctrl+O` → **Report a bug with diagnostics**. The visible shortcut should not be the only way to dismiss an overlay.

## Assistant

You are correct. Amp’s interactive TUI uses an alternate screen, so normal terminal scrollback is unavailable. There is currently no documented setting to disable it.

Best immediate workaround: open [this thread in your browser](https://ampcode.com/threads/T-01a0af2c-b657-729d-8d1f-9627697f907f). The complete transcript will remain scrollable there.

Inside the TUI:

- Mouse wheel should scroll Amp’s internal transcript.
- `Home` jumps to the top.
- `End` jumps to the bottom.
- `Ctrl+O` → **thread: open in browser** avoids the problem.

For terminal output without the full-screen interface, quit and use:

```powershell
amp -x "your question"
```

That prints the final response into normal terminal scrollback. Do **not** use `--no-tui`; that starts a remote runner rather than a normal chat.

## Assistant

The cause is in GhostShell, not Amp:

- GhostShell globally sets `force_main_screen: true`, stripping Amp’s alternate-screen sequence ([settings](file:///C:/Users/donal/projects/GhostShell/ai_terminal.sublime-settings#L108-L111)).
- Amp still renders a fixed-screen TUI, so no lines enter GhostShell’s scrollback.
- Because the alternate-screen signal was stripped, GhostShell also steals PageUp/PageDown instead of forwarding them ([routing](file:///C:/Users/donal/projects/GhostShell/ai_terminal.py#L2483-L2492)).
- The Amp profile has no TUI overrides; it only disables animation ([profile](file:///C:/Users/donal/projects/GhostShell/ai_terminal.sublime-settings#L165-L187)).

Recommended Amp profile:

```json
"Amp": {
    "detachable": true,
    "launch_command": ["amp"],
    "force_main_screen": false,
    "page_keys_to_pty": true,
    "mouse_handling": true,
    "wheel_to_pty": true,
    "spawn_env": {
        "NO_ANIMATION": "1"
    }
}
```

This restores Amp’s genuine alternate screen and sends scrolling input to Amp. It does **not** create native Sublime scrollback; Amp must scroll its own transcript.

`scrollback_history_size` cannot solve this: alternate-screen rows are intentionally excluded from history. Also, GhostShell’s Tune Profile description for `force_main_screen` is backwards at [line 9348](file:///C:/Users/donal/projects/GhostShell/ai_terminal.py#L9347-L9349).

## Assistant

Because GhostShell has **no `Ctrl+.` key binding**.

It binds `.` and many Ctrl combinations, but omitted `ctrl+.`. Therefore Sublime never forwards the keystroke to Amp.

I verified GhostShell’s encoder supports it correctly as `ESC[46;5u`; only the keymap entry is missing. This is a GhostShell bug, and adding one binding should fix it.

## Assistant

GhostShell **already forces Amp onto the main screen** by stripping `?1049` ([setting](file:///C:/Users/donal/projects/GhostShell/ai_terminal.sublime-settings#L108-L111)). The problem is that Amp does not change rendering styles: it continues repainting a fixed TUI matrix. Stripping the alternate-screen command cannot convert that matrix into scrolling output.

Amp itself has no interactive main-screen option. Current v0.0.1789639648 offers:

- Full-screen interactive TUI
- `amp -x` noninteractive output
- `--no-tui`, which is only a remote runner

Database review found stale/incomplete Amp data:

- Eight recordings; normal launches consistently request alternate screen and mouse tracking.
- Zero Amp settings recorded.
- Only two shortcuts stored, despite notes listing many more.
- `mouse_handling.current_value` says `true`, but the current profile has no override.
- No `force_main_screen` assessment exists.

A proper solution requires Amp to add an inline/main-screen renderer like Claude Code’s `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ALTERNATE_SCREEN`. GhostShell cannot manufacture scrollback from Amp’s repeated fixed-screen redraws.

## Assistant

You’re right. The Amp audit was incomplete, yet Amp inherited a global behavior that rewrites terminal output.

What happened:

- `force_main_screen` predates the Amp profile.
- It globally removes VT modes `47`, `1047`, and `1049` before libghostty sees them.
- Amp was added later without verified TUI settings, so it inherited this stripping accidentally.
- The database confirms the Amp walk was incomplete and contains stale/conflicting conclusions.

This is an architectural hack, not true main-screen support. It works acceptably only when the application itself offers an inline renderer, as Claude Code does. For Amp, it produces the broken fixed-frame/no-scrollback hybrid you experienced.

The proper direction is:

1. Stop defaulting `force_main_screen` to true globally.
2. Use per-profile overrides only where live testing proves them correct.
3. Use each CLI’s native main-screen option when available.
4. Make GhostShell’s toolbar usable with genuine alternate-screen applications.

I cannot determine from Git who personally authored it—the commits are all attributed to your Git identity—but it entered GhostShell before Amp and was applied to Amp without a proper audit.

Not\r\n9354: # offered as toggles here for that reason -- listed so the \"why doesn't\r\n9355: # Respawn pick this up\" question has an answer in one place.\r\n9356: _RELAUNCH_REQUIRED_PROFILE_KEYS = (\r\n9357:     \"spawn_env\",\r\n9358:     \"launch_command\",\r\n9359:     \"detachable\",  # controls how *future* spawns of this profile behave, not this one\r\n9360: )\r\n9361: \r\n9362: \r\n9363: def _toggle_profile_bool(profile_name, key, default):\r\n9364:     \"\"\"Flip one boolean in profile_name's explicit override dict and persist\r\n9365:     it to ai_terminal.sublime-settings's \"profiles\" key. It closes this plugin's pipe handles but\r\n8895:     # leaves the broker and its child process untouched.\r\n8896:     pty.kill()\r\n8897: \r\n8898:     if view_is_usable:\r\n8899:         target = old_view\r\n8900:     else:\r\n10391: \r\n10392: \r\n10393: class AiTerminalNoopCommand(sublime_plugin.TextCommand):\r\n10394:     \"\"\"Do nothing (placeholder no-op command).\r\n10395: \r\n10396:     No key/menu/palette binding; invoked programmatically.\r\n10397:     \"\"\"\r\n10398: \r\n10399:     def run(self, edit):\r\n10400:         pass\r\n10401: \r\n10402: \r\n10403: class AiTerminalTrackpadScrollCommand(sublime_plugin.TextCommand):\r\n10404:     \"\"\"Receive mouse-wheel / two-finger trackpad via the mousemap.\r\n10405: \r\n10406:     ST's Default (Windows) mousemap does not bind bare scroll_up/scroll_down;\r\n10407:     the core pans the view instead, and scroll_lines is often never fired (or\r\n10408:     fires once then dies when content fits). On any\r\n10410:     other view: fall through to native scroll_lines so normal editors still\r\n10411:     scroll.\r\n10412:     \"\"\"\r\n10413: \r\n10414:     def run(self, edit, direction=\"up\", amount=3.0):\r\n10415:         view = self.view\r\n10416:         try:\r\n10417:             amt = abs(float(amount))\r\n10418:         except (TypeError, ValueError):\r\n10419:             amt = 3.0\r\n10420:         if amt <= 0:\r\n10421:             amt = 1.0\r\n10422:         # ST scroll_lines: positive = content moves down = \"scroll up\"\r\n10423:         signed = amt if direction == \"up\" else -amt\r\n10424: \r\n10425:         if not view.settings().get(_VIEW_SETTING):\r\n10426:             view.run_command(\"scroll_lines\", {\"amount\": signed})\r\n10427:             return\r\n10428: \r\n10429:         term = _Terminal.from_id(view.id())\r\n10430:         if term is None or not _wheel_to_pty_enabled(term):\r\n10431:             view.run_command(\"scroll_lines\", {\"amount\": signed})\r\n10432:             return\r\n10433: \r\n10434:         _route_mouse_wheel(view, term, signed)\r\n10435:         _pin_terminal_viewport(view, term)\r\n10436:         sublime.set_timeout(\r\n10437:             lambda v=view, t=term: _pin_terminal_viewport(v, t), 0\r\n10438:         )\r\n10439: \r\n10440: \r\n10441: class AiTerminalDumpScreenCommand(sublime_plugin.TextCommand):\r\n10442:     \"\"\"Print the current screen grid and cursor to the ST console for debugging.\r\n10443: \r\n10444:     No key/menu/palette binding; invoked programmatically (debug).\r\n10445:     \"\"\"\r\n10446: \r\n10447:     def run(self, edit):\r\n10448:         term = _Terminal.from_id(self.view.id())\r\n10449:         if not term:\r\n10450:             print(\"[ai_terminal] no terminal for this view\")\r\n10451:             return\r\n10452:         with term._lock:\r\n10453:             print(f\"[ai_terminal] cursor=({term.screen.x},{term.screen.y}) \"\r\n10454:                   f\"size=({term.screen.cols}x{term.screen.rows}) \"\r\n10455:                   f\"alt={term.screen.alt_screen} \"\r\n10456:                   f\"sgr=fg={term.parser._fg} bg={term.parser._bg} \"\r\n10457:                   f\"flags={term.parser._flags}\")\r\n10458:             for r, row in enumerate(term.screen.grid):\r\n10459:                 ar = term.screen.attrs[r]\r\n10460:                 marks = \"\".join(\"*\" if a else \" \" for a in ar)\r\n10461:                 print(f\"  {r:2d}|{''.join(row)}|\")\r\n10462:                 print(f\"     {marks}|  (attrs: * = non-default)\")\r\n10463: \r\n10464: \r\n10465: # ─── hover-motion polling (mode 1003 \"any-event\" mouse tracking) ──────────────\r\n10466: #\r\n10467: # ST's plugin API has no continuous mouse-move event. EventListener.on_hover\r\n10468: # is the only mouse-position hook plugins get outside of click/drag/scroll\r\n10469: # commands, and it is debounced/settle-based, not a live stream -- confirmed\r\n10470: # empirically (2026-08-05): continuous mouse movement over an ST view produced\r\n10471: # only 4 on_hover calls in 10s (~every 2.4-5.1s), nowhere near real-time. Apps\r\n10472: # that enable xterm mode 1003 (Textual's hover-highlight, e.g. pybackup's TUI)\r\n10473: # need a report for every cell the cursor crosses, which on_hover cannot give.\r\n10474: #\r\n10475: # plugin_host is a real, unsandboxed Python process though, so instead of\r\n10476: # waiting on ST's event system this polls the actual OS cursor position via\r\n10477: # user32.GetCursorPos on a fast timer and forwards synthetic xterm motion\r\n10478: # reports directly -- independent of anything ST chooses to deliver. Windows-\r\n10479: # only (ctypes user32); no-ops elsewhere since ai_terminal targets Windows.\r\n10480: #\r\n10481: # Scope/known limitation: only forwards hover for window.active_view() of the\r\n10482: # OS foreground ST window. A terminal visible in a background pane/window\r\n10483: # while another view has focus will not receive hover motion -- acceptable\r\n10484: # because a user can only be pointing at what has focus/foreground in practice\r\n10485: # for this use case (hover-driven TUI widget highlighting).\r\n10486: \r\n10487: _HOVER_POLL_MS = 33  # ~30Hz -- reads as continuous; early-exits keep it cheap when idle\r\n10488: _hover_poll_token = None\r\n10489: _hover_last_cell = {}  # view_id -> (col, row) last cell a motion report was sent for\r\n10490: \r\n10491: \r\n10492: class _POINT(ctypes.Structure):\r\n10493:     _fields_ = [(\"x\", ctypes.c_long), (\"y\", ctypes.c_long)]\r\n10494: \r\n10495: \r\n10496: def _hover_st_hwnd():\r\n10497:     \"\"\"HWND of the OS foreground window, if it's a Sublime Text window.\"\"\"\r\n10498:     try:\r\n10499:         u32 = ctypes.windll.user32\r\n10500:         hwnd = u32.GetForegroundWindow()\r\n10501:         if not hwnd:\r\n10502:             return None\r\n10503:         buf = ctypes.create_unicode_buffer(64)\r\n10504:         u32.GetClassNameW(hwnd, buf, 64)\r\n10505:         if buf.value != \"PX_WINDOW_CLASS\":\r\n10506:             return None\r\n10507:         return hwnd\r\n10508:     except (OSError, AttributeError):\r\n10509:         print(\"[ai_terminal] hover: foreground-window lookup failed:\\n%s\"\r\n10510:               % traceback.format_exc())\r\n10511:         return None\r\n10512: \r\n10513: \r\n10514: def _hover_poll_tick():\r\n10515:     hwnd = _hover_st_hwnd()\r\n10516:     if hwnd is None:\r\n10517:         return\r\n10518:     win = sublime.active_window()\r\n10519:     view = win.active_view() if win else None\r\n10520:     if view is None:\r\n10521:         return\r\n10522:     term = _Terminal.from_id(view.id())\r\n10523:     if term is None:\r\n10524:         return\r\n10525:     if not _mouse_handling_enabled(term):\r\n10526:         return\r\n10527:     if int(term.screen.mouse_tracking or 0) < 1003:\r\n10528:         return  # clicks/drag already routed via _route_mouse_click; only \"any-event\" needs hover\r\n10529: \r\n10530:     u32 = ctypes.windll.user32\r\n10531:     pt = _POINT()\r\n10532:     if not u32.GetCursorPos(ctypes.byref(pt)):\r\n10533:         return\r\n10534:     client = _POINT(pt.x, pt.y)\r\n10535:     if not u32.ScreenToClient(hwnd, ctypes.byref(client)):\r\n10536:         return\r\n10537:     try:\r\n10538:         text_pt = view.window_to_text((client.x, client.y))\r\n10539:         row, col = view.rowcol(text_pt)\r\n10540:     except (RuntimeError, AttributeError, TypeError):\r\n10541:         print(\"[ai_terminal] hover: point-to-text lookup failed:\\n%s\"\r\n10542:               % traceback.format_exc())\r\n10543:         return\r\n10544:     cell = _view_point_to_cell(\r\n10545:         row, col,\r\n10546:         hist_len=_mouse_hist_len(term),\r\n10547:         screen_rows=term.screen.rows,\r\n10548:         screen_cols=term.screen.cols,\r\n10549:     )\r\n10550:     if cell is None:\r\n10551:         return\r\n10552:     vid = view.id()\r\n10553:     if _hover_last_cell.get(vid) == cell:\r\n10554:         return\r\n10555:     _hover_last_cell[vid] = cell\r\n10556:     col, row = cell\r\n10557:     try:\r\n10558:         sgr = term.screen.mouse_sgr\r\n10559:         seq = _encode_mouse(_BTN_RELEASE_X10, col, row, press=True, motion=True, sgr=sgr)\r\n10560:         term.send_string(seq)\r\n10561:     except Exception as e:\r\n10562:         print(f\"[ai_terminal] hover motion send failed: {e}\")\r\n10563: \r\n10564: \r\n10565: def _hover_poll_loop():\r\n10566:     global _hover_poll_token\r\n10567:     try:\r\n10568:         if os.name == \"nt\":\r\n10569:             _hover_poll_tick()\r\n10570:     except Exception as e:\r\n10571:         print(f\"[ai_terminal] hover poll error: {e}\")\r\n10572:     _hover_poll_token = sublime.set_timeout(_hover_poll_loop, _HOVER_POLL_MS)\r\n10573: \r\n10574: \r\n10575: # ─── viewport clamp ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\r\n10576: #\r\n10577: # ST's view.show() overshoots to a NEGATIVE viewport y (e.g. vp[1]=-20) when\r\n10578: # content fits the viewport -- it tries to \"nicely\" position the caret and\r\n10579: # overshoots because there's nothing to scroll. Our own render clamps this, but\r\n10580: # ST ALSO calls view.show internally on view focus/hover -- mouse entering the\r\n10581: # view bbox triggers it BETWEEN renders. During generation a render clamps it\r\n10582: # within ~110ms, but when Claude is idle there's no TUI output -> no render ->\r\n10583: # the -20 persists until the next TUI frame (cursor blink ~500ms), so the user\r\n10584: # sees the text dip one line for ~500ms then snap back. This loop clamps vp to\r\n10585: # (0,0) whenever content fits, independent of the render clock, killing the dip\r\n10586: # within 16ms. It only fires when content fits (le <= ve), so it never fights\r\n10587: # the user scrolling up to read scrollback when content exceeds the viewport.\r\n10588: \r\n10589: _clamp_token = None\r\n10590: \r\n10591: \r\n10592: def _vp_pan_to_tui_scroll(view, term, dy_from_rest):\r\n10593:     \"\"\"Turn ST viewport drift from rest into PTY scroll — content-grab model.\r\n10594: \r\n10595:     dy_from_rest = viewport_y - rest_y (rest = top of real TUI, below top pad).\r\n10596: \r\n10597:       dy > 0  text slides UP   → reveal newer below → amount < 0\r\n10598:       dy < 0  text slides DOWN → reveal older above → amount > 0\r\n10599: \r\n10600:     Opposite of the TUI scroll-button (view move). Both signs must work:\r\n10601:     rest is not y=0 so finger-down can produce dy < 0.\r\n10602:     \"\"\"\r\n10603:     lh = view.line_height() or 12.0\r\n10604:     dy = float(dy_from_rest)\r\n10605:     if abs(dy) < 1.5:\r\n10606:         return False\r\n10607:     now = time.time()\r\n10608:     last = float(getattr(term, \"_last_scroll_send_t\", 0.0) or 0.0)\r\n10609:     if (now - last) < 0.08:\r\n10610:         return False\r\n10611:     ticks = 1 if abs(dy) < lh * 0.75 else 2\r\n10612:     # Content-grab: text moves with fingers.\r\n10613:     amount = -float(ticks) if dy > 0 else float(ticks)\r\n10614:     term._last_user_pan_t = now\r\n10615:     try:\r\n10616:         n = int(getattr(term, \"_vp_pan_log_n\", 0) or 0)\r\n10617:         if n < 8:\r\n10618:             print(\r\n10619:                 f\"[ai_terminal] content-grab pan→TUI \"\r\n10620:                 f\"dy_rest={dy:.1f}px steps={ticks} \"\r\n10621:                 f\"({'older' if amount > 0 else 'newer'})\"\r\n10622:             )\r\n10623:             term._vp_pan_log_n = n + 1\r\n10624:         _route_mouse_wheel(view, term, amount)\r\n10625:         return True\r\n10626:     except Exception as e:\r\n10627:         print(f\"[ai_terminal] vp-pan scroll failed: {e}\")\r\n10628:         return False\r\n10629: \r\n10630: \r\n10631: def _clamp_vp_loop():\r\n10632:     global _clamp_token\r\n10633:     try:\r\n10634:         for _vid, term in list(_term_registry().items()):\r\n10635:             v = term.view\r\n10636:             if not v or not v.is_valid():\r\n10637:                 continue\r\n10638:             # Every ai_terminal view: trackpad = core pan. Convert + pin.\r\n10639:             # (Previously gated on alt/mouse only; force_main_screen makes\r\n10640:             # alt_screen False even under Grok, and a missed mouse mode left\r\n10641:             # pure pan with no PTY traffic — matches empty wheel casts.)\r\n10642:             try:\r\n10643:                 v.settings().set(\"scroll_past_end\", True)\r\n10644:             except (RuntimeError, AttributeError):\r\n10645:                 print(\"[ai_terminal] clamp-vp: scroll_past_end set failed:\\n%s\"\r\n10646:                       % traceback.format_exc())\r\n10647:             # Viewport HEIGHT change detector: catches show_panel/hide_panel\r\n10648:             # (console, find, ...), a window resize, sidebar/minimap toggle,\r\n10649:             # a tab-group sash drag -- anything that shrinks or grows this\r\n10650:             # view's viewport_extent(), not just an enumerable list of\r\n10651:             # commands. Nothing else in this plugin polls for this, and none\r\n10652:             # of it is a keystroke or new PTY output (the two things that\r\n10653:             # normally trigger the render loop's follow/pin recompute), so a\r\n10654:             # view that was scrolled/pinned to the tail at the OLD height\r\n10655:             # keeps that same viewport y against the new height -- reported\r\n10656:             # live as the console panel hiding the last several lines of a\r\n10657:             # tab that was following. Already-running 8ms loop, so this adds\r\n10658:             # no new timer.\r\n10659:             try:\r\n10660:                 ve_now_h = float(v.viewport_extent()[1])\r\n10661:             except (RuntimeError, AttributeError, TypeError):\r\n10662:                 ve_now_h = None\r\n10663:             if ve_now_h is not None:\r\n10664:                 last_ve_h = getattr(term, \"_last_ve_h\", None)\r\n10665:                 if last_ve_h is None:\r\n10666:                     term._last_ve_h = ve_now_h\r\n10667:                 elif abs(ve_now_h - last_ve_h) <= 0.5:\r\n10668:                     # Matches the confirmed height -- also resets a candidate\r\n10669:                     # that didn't pan out (one noisy tick, not a real change).\r\n10670:                     term._ve_h_candidate = None\r\n10671:                     term._ve_h_candidate_count = 0\r\n10672:                 else:\r\n10673:                     # Differs from the confirmed height. Requires the SAME\r\n10674:                     # new value on 2 consecutive ticks (16ms) before acting --\r\n10675:                     # mirrors _LayoutWatcher's own debounce/confirm pattern\r\n10676:                     # for the identical class of bug (that one guards PTY\r\n10677:                     # resize against transient content-width/scrollbar\r\n10678:                     # jitter; this guards a viewport write against the same\r\n10679:                     # kind of single-tick noise on the height axis). Without\r\n10680:                     # this, a real single-frame layout jitter during active\r\n10681:                     # typing/streaming was misread as a genuine panel/layout\r\n10682:                     # change on every such frame, each one forcing a\r\n10683:                     # _scroll_to_bottom viewport write -- reported live as\r\n10684:                     # jiggling and slow key response while typing.\r\n10685:                     candidate = getattr(term, \"_ve_h_candidate\", None)\r\n10686:                     if candidate is not None and abs(ve_now_h - candidate) <= 0.5:\r\n10687:                         term._ve_h_candidate_count = (\r\n10688:                             int(getattr(term, \"_ve_h_candidate_count\", 0)) + 1\r\n10689:                         )\r\n10690:                     else:\r\n10691:                         term._ve_h_candidate = ve_now_h\r\n10692:                         term._ve_h_candidate_count = 1\r\n10693:                     if term._ve_h_candidate_count >= 2:\r\n10694:                         term._last_ve_h = ve_now_h\r\n10695:                         term._ve_h_candidate = None\r\n10696:                         term._ve_h_candidate_count = 0\r\n10697:                         _resync_viewport_after_height_change(v, term)\r\n10698:                         continue\r\n10699:             try:\r\n10700:                 vp = v.viewport_position()\r\n10701:                 rest = _host_rest_y(v)\r\n10702:                 dy_rest = float(vp[1]) - rest\r\n10703:                 dx = float(vp[0])\r\n10704:             except (RuntimeError, AttributeError, TypeError):\r\n10705:                 print(\"[ai_terminal] clamp-vp: viewport read failed:\\n%s\"\r\n10706:                       % traceback.format_exc())\r\n10707:                 continue\r\n10708: \r\n10709:             tui_like = _tui_like(term)\r\n10710:             try:\r\n10711:                 le = v.layout_extent()\r\n10712:                 ve = v.viewport_extent()\r\n10713:                 lh = v.line_height() or 12.0\r\n10714:                 # Near-fit relative to real content (pads always add height).\r\n10715:                 near_fit = _real_content_height(v) <= ve[1] + lh * 2\r\n10716:             except (RuntimeError, AttributeError, TypeError):\r\n10717:                 print(\"[ai_terminal] clamp-vp: layout measurement failed:\\n%s\"\r\n10718:                       % traceback.format_exc())\r\n10719:                 near_fit = False\r\n10720:                 lh = 12.0\r\n10721: \r\n10722:             if tui_like:\r\n10723:                 if near_fit:\r\n10724:                     # Short TUI pickers (for example Codex /hooks) are keyed\r\n10725:                     # with physical arrows. Sending pan→TUI keys on the first\r\n10732:                 # dy_rest=-pad_height injects Up arrows into Grok at t=0.\r\n10733:                 armed = bool(getattr(term, \"_vp_pan_armed\", False))\r\n10734:                 if not armed:\r\n10735:                     if abs(dy_rest) < 1.5 and abs(dx) < 0.5:\r\n10736:                         age = time.monotonic() - float(\r\n10737:                             getattr(term, \"_spawn_mono\", 0.0) or 0.0\r\n10738:                         )\r\n10739:                         if age >= 0.4:\r\n10740:                             term._vp_pan_armed = True\r\n10741:                     elif abs(dy_rest) >= 0.5 or abs(dx) >= 0.5:\r\n10742:                         _set_viewport(v, (0.0, rest), False)\r\n10743:                     continue\r\n10744:                 # Treat viewport displacement as an edge, not a level. ## Assistant

The core fault is confirmed: GhostShell currently rewrites the child’s VT stream and then repairs the resulting synthetic history. That is the opposite of a terminal emulator. I’m removing that entire path, not merely flipping its setting. I’m also replacing per-agent mouse/page routing guesses with protocol state: the application’s DEC modes will decide routing, as they do in normal terminals.

Stay on the applied size.\r\n        self.assertEqual(accepted_cols(32, 33), 32)\r\n\r\n    def test_shrink_by_one_column_is_applied(self):\r\n        # 33→32 fits; applying it is what kills the H-scrollbar / gutter chase.\r\n        self.assertEqual(accepted_cols(33, 32), 32)\r\n\r\n    def test_grow_by_two_or_more_is_a_real_resize(self):\r\n        self.assertEqual(accepted_cols(32, 34), 34)\r\n        self.assertEqual(accepted_cols(32, 55), 55)\r\n\r\n    def test_shrink_by_two_or_more_is_a_real_resize(self):\r\n        self.assertEqual(accepted_cols(55, 32), 32)\r\n\r\n    def test_32_33_attractor_locks_to_the_narrower_size(self):\r\n        cols = 33\r\n        for measured in (32, 33, 32, 33, 32, 33):\r\n            cols = accepted_cols(cols, measured)\r\n        self.assertEqual(cols, 32)\r\n\r\n\r\nclass GutterDigitDeltaTests(unittest.TestCase):\r\n    \"\"\"Cancel ST's real gutter-digit fluctuation with a fixed reservation.\r\n\r\n    ai/TODO.md \"4-digit gutter reserve\": ST's native line-number gutter\r\n    widens by a digit at every 10**n line-count boundary, so during an\r\n    active full-history replay that crosses one, usable_w -- and\r\n    therefore cols -- moves too, retriggering a PTY resize that restarts\r\n    the replay at the new width, crossing the boundary again. ## Assistant

The earlier SText history confirms this was not a clean terminal design that later broke accidentally: the very first libghostty integration already intercepted alternate-screen sequences. I’m using the simpler terminal contract—not reverting to that historical implementation. I also found the terminal view deliberately enabled Sublime line numbers and fold controls, then compensated with gutter-width and “minus four columns” heuristics. That is unlike Windows Terminal/Terminus and is being removed.

after, 1)\n+\n+    def test_net_reservation_is_pinned_to_cap_digit_width(self):\n+        cap = 2000\n+        for total_lines in (1, 9, 10, 99, 100, 999, 1000, 1999, 2000):\n+            delta = gutter_digit_delta(total_lines, cap)\n+            actual_digits = len(str(total_lines))\n+            self.assertEqual(actual_digits + delta, len(str(cap)))\n+\n+    def test_scrollback_cap_of_zero_is_treated_as_one_digit(self):\n+        self.assertEqual(gutter_digit_delta(5, 0), 0)\n+\n+\n+class FollowLineCountTests(unittest.TestCase):\n+    def test_default_keeps_the_full_count(self):\n+        self.assertEqual(follow_line_count(6), 6)\n+        self.assertEqual(follow_line_count(6, 0), 6)\n+\n+    def test_drops_configured_trailing_lines(self):\n+        self.assertEqual(follow_line_count(6, 2), 4)\n+        self.assertEqual(follow_line_count(6, 1), 5)\n+\n+    def test_does_not_go_below_zero(self):\n+        self.assertEqual(follow_line_count(1, 4), 0)\n+        self.assertEqual(follow_line_count(0, 2), 0)\n+\n+    def test_negative_ignore_is_treated_as_zero(self):\n+        self.assertEqual(follow_line_count(6, -2), 6)\n*** End Patch"
